scope: Seven compositions use only ordinary public Computable constructors. Three directed-MPFR residual families at 80 and 1100 bits, both signs, exact-zero controls, shared-child or independently reconstructed roots, three query orders and six shared allowances cover 468 valid schedules. Each schedule records bounded calls, every root fact after each call, unlimited retries, zero-work cached samples, finer requests and retries. Fifty-four invalid-descendant schedules use the same seven compositions. The real identities provide each root oracle from independently directed 2560-bit base enclosures; Python Fraction independently checks numerical containment. The unchanged corpus is replayed against the unretained runtime extraction.
limits: Constructors and structural-fact inspections can warm children outside explicit work allowances. Their fixed setup/order is part of each schedule, with no globally cold-process claim.
Round-tripping each root deliberately discards node caches and graph sharing; shared global constants may still be warm. The original child is then only a separately observed control.
Computable ln_1p is crate-private; this public corpus spells ln(1+x) through ordinary public add/ln and does not claim a native public Computable ln_1p API.
Input residuals satisfy abs(x)<2^-80 or 2^-1100, so the ln(1+x) and atanh identities stay in their real domains. acosh(cosh(x)) uses abs(x), and cancellation uses exact zero.
The corpus checks definite signs/zero/magnitude against the stated oracles and retains earlier exact-rational flags; it is not a complete proof of exact-rational recognition.

This is a finite sequential cross-root corpus, distinct from the prior thread stress and private publication tests. It does not establish general concurrency, full-board admission, formal whole-crate proofs or byte/time bounds.
Keep original process failures and full-size inputs. A failed process stops the phase without replacing its artifacts; any follow-up gets a separate phase and declared scope.
